insights.concise_text: The framework's conversational flow patterns are evaluated on 108 IQ2 debates where pre- and post-debate votes define winners, yielding Flow: 63% and Flow*: 65% accuracy.

triple.subject: conversational flow patterns
triple.object: 108 IQ2 debates with pre- and post-debate votes

insights.concise_text: Because Oxford-style debates disentangle conversational flow from audience prior leaning, the IQ2 winning-side delta labels provide the outcome used to test flow features.

triple.subject: Oxford-style debates
triple.object: pre- and post-debate votes to define winning-side delta labels

insights.concise_text: The opening statements that identify talking points before interaction enable the log-odds ratio method to define own and opposing talking points from introduction word usage.

triple.subject: opening statements
triple.object: introduction word usage for log-odds ratio talking points

insights.concise_text: The number of discussion points adopted, modeled as words adopted by opponents at least twice, is selected most often in Flow* with positive regression coefficients.

triple.subject: the number of discussion points adopted
triple.object: words adopted by opponents at least twice to Flow* positive regression coefficients

insights.concise_text: The finding that eventual winners adopt more opponent discussion points is supported by 78% of valid discussion points being picked up by the opposing side to be challenged.

triple.subject: 78% of the valid discussion points picked up to be challenged
triple.object: eventual winners adopt more opponent discussion points

insights.concise_text: The drop in self-coverage and larger drop in summed coverage for winning teams become predictive Flow features through the drop in usage of own talking points with positive coefficients.

triple.subject: drop in self-coverage for winning teams
triple.object: Flow* prediction via positive coefficients

insights.concise_text: Audience features use applause and laughter counts as rough outcome indicators because winning teams tend to receive more laughter during discussion and more applause during conclusion.

triple.subject: applause and laughter counts
triple.object: Audience features as rough outcome indicators

insights.concise_text: Flow features outperform length and BOW baselines despite excluding the concluding round, where winning teams tend to receive more applause.

triple.subject: Flow features
triple.object: length and BOW baselines without the concluding round

insights.concise_text: The basic unigram-based definition of discussion points limits the robustness of idea flow analysis because it does not account for context or semantic sense.

triple.subject: basic unigram-based definition of discussion points
triple.object: robustness of idea flow analysis

insights.concise_text: The paper's focus on conversational flow extends previous influence studies in relatively unstructured political settings by using highly structured Oxford-style debates that control for confounding factors.

triple.subject: conversational flow in Oxford-style debates
triple.object: previous influence studies in relatively unstructured political settings
